product_family: FigJam is Figma's collaborative whiteboard product included with all Figma subscription plans. FigJam AI refers to the suite of AI-powered features (Figma Make, content summarization, template generation) available across all Figma products including Figma Design, FigJam, Dev Mode, Figma Slides, and others. Not a standalone product; AI capabilities are built into the broader Figma platform.

privacy.ai_training_note: Figma has configurable content training settings with different defaults by plan tier: (1) Starter & Professional plans have content training enabled by default (admins can opt out in team settings). (2) Organization & Enterprise plans have content training disabled by default (admins can enable if needed). (3) Education and Government accounts are never used for training. When content training is enabled, Figma may use customer content to train machine learning and AI models to improve and enhance products. Data is de-identified and redacted to remove sensitive information from text and images. Third-party AI vendors (including OpenAI) are explicitly prohibited from using Figma customer data for their own model training. Free Community files are not trained on until Figma decides and transparently communicates an approach to attribution. Users can disable content training at any time, and new content added after disabling will not be used for training.

flags: FigJam AI is not a standalone product: FigJam is a Figma collaborative whiteboard product included with all plans, and 'FigJam AI' refers to AI features available across Figma products, so this listing covers Figma's AI features rather than a separate product.

There is a critical governance difference between plans: Starter and Professional plans have content training on by default (users must opt out), while Organization and Enterprise plans have it off by default (admins must opt in). This is a material difference in data usage posture across customer tiers.
Figma explicitly prohibits PHI/HIPAA data in its Acceptable Use Policy; organizations requiring HIPAA compliance should not use Figma for health information workflows.
TISAX is listed on the security page but only at the 'participation' stage, with the audit still in progress; it is not yet certified.

A January 2020 blog post mentioned only SOC 2 Type II at that time, while the current security page (2026) claims ISO 27001/27017/27018/27701 with annual audit cycles, suggesting these were achieved or recertified after 2020; request current audit reports to verify.

Figma's DPA, last updated March 30, 2026, applies broadly to the 'Figma Platform' but does not explicitly enumerate per-product coverage (FigJam vs. Figma Design vs. Figma Make, etc.); users seeking product-specific data handling details should contact Figma.
Education and Government account data is explicitly never used for AI training, ensuring public sector and educational use cases are protected from content training.
Free Community files are not currently used for AI training pending transparent communication on the attribution approach; this is good practice, but users should watch for changes.
The free tier has restricted community file access and may have different data handling terms than paid plans; free users should review those terms.
